briefing.text: Information Technology still leads sector attention on all three feeds: news buzz 82.4 (down 4.0 on the day, flat over 7 days; mentions down 75%, sentiment 0.09; NVDA, MSFT, AMD, CRWV, AVGO), X buzz 93.0 (down 0.5; mentions down 5%; NVDA, MU, AMD, MSFT, IREN) and Reddit buzz 93.7 (down 1.2, up 0.9 on the week; mentions down 56%; NVDA, MSFT, TSM, AMD, AAPL). On news, the biggest drops were Financials (66.5, down 13.9, from rank 7 to 11; BAC, UBS, BLK, C, MS) and Energy (69.0, down 11.3, 7-day change down 6.5; VTOL, XOM, ENB). On X, Healthcare rose 12.7 to 39.8 (sentiment 0.63, driven by WWB), Financial Services rose 11.0 to 37.2 (BITW, mentions up 100%) and Utilities rose 1.5 to 84.9 (mentions up 125%; NFE, EIX, AES). On Reddit, Financial Services gained 1.8 (up 9.7 over the week; mentions up 47%; fund tickers such as FSKAX, VTIAX) while Health Care slipped 3.9 to 83.0.

DPZ #1: its news is a generic analyst-upgrades roundup (benzinga, 2 of 4 articles positive), so news does not explain the rank; X attention does.
SHAK #2: no news in the file; the rank comes from X mentions (65) and a 3.2% daily gain.
TAP #3: only 1 news mention; no headline in the file, so news does not explain the rank.
UAL #4: 13 articles, none positive; flights canceled and delayed as air travel recovers from the shutdown, plus a $30.1 billion upgrade request. This explains the attention and the KPI market.
SCHW #5: 8 articles, but the headlines are about crypto and market pullbacks, not clearly Schwab-specific, so weak support.
HD #7: headline is the week-ahead roundup naming HD earnings on 11-17, which fits the catalyst tag.
DIS #8: a $7.5 billion fund buying it (sentiment 0.82) and the same earnings-week roundup (earnings 11-17).
PEP #9: dividend-stock pieces, mixed sentiment (3 positive, 3 negative); explains some attention, not the move.

DPZ (Domino's) takes #1 with a score of 0.92, new to the ranking this pull. Its attention is 2.37 above normal overall and 2.91 on X (both top-percentile), with 81 X mentions; volume is slightly above normal (0.15) and the price moved 1.4 sigmas on a 2.5% gain. SHAK (Shake Shack, #2, up from 4) has similar attention (2.03 overall, 2.70 on X) with volume near normal (-0.09) and a 1.0 sigma move on a 3.2% gain. TAP (Molson Coors, #3, up from 16) shows attention 1.45 and X attention 1.96, with a 1.15 sigma move on a 3.2% gain. None of the three has a catalyst tag, and the top two are ranked mainly on attention, which carries 70% of the score weight.

notes: Ranks are by the scoring of record (pick_rank, w2). Prices and moves as of the last pull of the day. Facts from public data; not investment advice.
